stoppingDecision.assessment: Three related UCR options give a broad philosophical foundation, an applied ethics and politics direction, and a mind and cognition direction. The historically organised approach shares much of the broad option’s philosophical and interpretive work and is not included because three options already meet the limit.

analysis: The broad option keeps the disciplinary core of introduction, ethics, mind, emotion, and free will, with political philosophy, formal logic, argument and interpretive courses. The additional options retain a philosophical core and diverge in their primary questions and methods. The ethics option studies political authority and responsibility through law, human rights, institutions and collective action. The theoretical option studies consciousness, identity, agency and meaning through mind, logic, psycholinguistics and empirical and computational approaches. In the current workbook the two cases of legal and rhetorical course timing are fixed by swapping Criminal Law with Modern Sociology and Rhetoric in Action with Perspectives on Literary Meaning. Brain and Behavior in the first autumn precedes Psycholinguistics in its only planned spring, swapped with Neurobiology. No course selection changes. Description-only Perspectives on Literary Meaning gives real interpretive practice and an independent project but does not teach the comparator’s global philosophical hermeneutics. Description-only Perception and Action supplies empirical study of perception and action and complements philosophy of mind. History of Philosophy was tested through the five philosophy courses and the historical, heritage and interpretive palette. It is a coherent direction with substantial overlap with the broad response. Three options already occupy the permitted slots. The eight original comparisons were reconsidered, with seven positive pairings retained. European Union Politics concerns institutions and empirical legislative research and is no longer equated with advanced political philosophy. Dedicated epistemology, philosophy of science and advanced historical courses remain visible gaps.
